chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Ḥamzah ibn Ḥumrān, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who emancipates half of his slave-girl, then accuses her of zina. He said: “I hold that fifty lashes are upon him, and that he should seek Allah’s forgiveness.” I said: What if she declares him absolved and pardons him? He said: “There is no beating upon him if she pardons him before she brings the matter forward.” I said: Does she cover her head from him when he emancipates half of her? He said: “Yes, and she performs salat while her head is covered, and she does not marry until she pays what is due upon her or he emancipates the other half.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What the beginning of the report contains, that he accused her after emancipating half of her, is to be understood as meaning that he had emancipated five-eighths of her, because by that he would deserve fifty lashes. But if the half was exactly equal, then no more than forty are due upon him, because that is half of the hadd. It is also possible that he deserved forty on account of what he had emancipated of her, and whatever exceeds that is by way of ta'zir, because whoever accuses a slave deserves ta'zir even if he does not deserve the hadd, as we have explained.

key_terms.خَمْسِينَ جَلْدَةً: fifty lashes as the stated punishment
key_terms.فِي حِلٍّ: in a state of absolution from her claim
key_terms.قَذَفَهَا: he accused her of zina falsely

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man falsely accuses his partially emancipated slave-girl of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings concerning a partially emancipated slave-girl who is accused of zina by her owner. It addresses the punishment for false accusation, the effect of her pardon before formal litigation, and rulings related to her covering and marriage after partial emancipation. The closing note clarifies how the legal penalty is calculated in light of her degree of freedom.
